item.title: Half of rental agents willing to exclude foreign tenants: study
item.description:
Half of rental agents willing to exclude foreign tenants: study

November 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Almost half of rental agents contacted for a government-commissioned study were willing to discriminate against potential tenants with foreign roots, researchers have found.

The study, conducted by the Verwey-Jonker Institute, used actors posing as landlords to phone rental agents and ask them if they could avoid renting to “foreigners; Moroccans, Turks or Poles”.

They found that 97 out of 200 agreed outright with the request. Another 30% didn’t refuse, mostly saying it was up to the landlord, and only 20% said no.

“Expat” privileges

In 36 of the cases, agents distinguished “expats” as good foreign tenants, describing them as highly educated and well paid, with reliable employers. Some also said they tend to leave after a while, which they presented as a way around the 2024 ban on most temporary leases.

“Let me put your mind at rest, neither do we,” one agent told an actor who said they did not have a good feeling about foreigners. “The foreigners we usually talk about are the expats, who just come here to work for the big companies.”

Another said: “Officially we’re not allowed to discriminate, of course, but if you say you don’t want people from certain types of countries, I don’t need to put them forward to you.”

Moroccan-sounding names 

In separate tests on 1,662 listings on the rental site Pararius between December and May, applicants with Moroccan-sounding names were invited to viewings less often than otherwise identical applicants with Dutch-sounding names.

For men, there were 14% of cases where only the Dutch-named applicant got an invitation, and 16% for women. Last year’s monitor found no significant discrimination against any group for the first time. The researchers found none this year against Polish-sounding names or same-sex couples.

Findings of the investigations were sent to MPs on Wednesday.

item.title: Back to class: cabinet seeks to train civil servants as teachers
item.description:
Back to class: cabinet seeks to train civil servants as teachers

November 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A majority of MPs are seeking to have soon-to-be-redundant civil servants at the education, culture and science ministry (OCW) retrained as teachers.

The VVD will bring the proposal, which also has the backing of political parties D66, CDA, JA21 and 50Plus, the to the cabinet Thursday.

VVD MP Arend Kisteman believes the plan will “kill two birds with one stone”.

“The announced cuts are a great opportunity to have these enthusiastic people voluntarily retrained for a job in education at the expense of the government,” Kisteman told broadcaster NOS.

The cabinet plans to eliminate 25,000 civil servants over the next nine years, a cut of some 16% by 2035. The OCW will not be spared.

Supporters say retraining already enthusiastic education workers as teachers will help alleviate chronic teacher shortages nationwide, especially in the country’s big cities.

But similar past initiatives have gotten low marks over schools’ reluctance to hire people with little to no classroom experience and civil servants’ reluctance to take salary cuts.

item.title: Disgruntled estate agents plan rival to property site Funda
item.description:
Disgruntled estate agents plan rival to property site Funda

November 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A group of disgruntled real estate brokers is starting a rival online real estate marketplace to the dominant Funda, saying it is “building a platform in which the broker is no longer a cash cow but is at the helm.”

The new platform, called Homek, is expected to launch in March 2027. For now, it’s appealing to brokers to join the platform, with RTL Z reporting that it won’t launch until at least 1,000 agents have bought in or the foundation has raised €1 million.

The increasing price of placing a property on Funda is one of the irritants that led the brokers to start the rival site.

“Homek is the fair, transparent alternative to Funda, without expensive packages or paid priority,” says Homek’s website, which currently doesn’t list any properties for sale or rent.

Only certified brokers affiliated with industry associations can use Homek, unlike Funda, where unaffiliated real estate agents who meet the site’s conditions can place properties.

Brokers on Homek will also share in the profits.

“The high placement costs and priority paid at Funda require an alternative: a housing platform where real estate agents themselves are in charge,” says Homek’s website. It promises “fair rates, equal opportunities and control for the affiliated brokers and offices.”

Supply problems

Funda was established in 2001 by the brokers’ association NVM.

“As brokers, we came up with Funda ourselves,” says Toine Naber, former chairman of the NVM branch in West-Brabant and a past member of Funda’s advisory board. “With Homek, we get the chance to do it again, but this time without giving away control of our own future.”

Sven Heinen, who is slated to be chairman of the Homek Foundation, told RTL Z he recognises that to become successful, Homek must have the goods to offer home buyers or renters.

“In the past, there have been plenty of competitors of Funda who wanted to take a piece of this market, but they all stalled because the supply was too limited,” Heinen says. “Only when many real estate agents join us and share their housing supply…can we become a serious competitor of Funda.”

Heinen says that within 48 hours, they’ve already raised €200,000.

Funda says it’s not worried about the competition for now. “In a healthy market, there is competition, and sometimes new players join,” spokesperson Claire Verhagen told RTL Z. “We look forward to that with confidence.”

item.title: Coalition parties ready to vote against each other on tax plans
item.description:
Coalition parties ready to vote against each other on tax plans

November 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The ruling coalition parties have signalled they could vote against one another on amendments to the 2027 tax plan before parliament votes on it next week, after a debate that went ran late into Wednesday night.

Prime minister Rob Jetten’s centrist social-liberal D66 and the centrist Christian Democrat CDA said they could back opposition amendments even if their coalition partner, the right-wing liberal VVD, voted against them, broadcaster NOS reported.

“It is not an unthinkable situation,” D66 finance spokesman Henk-Jan Oosterhuis said after repeated questions from MPs. “The coalition is not a merger party.” CDA MP Inge van Dijk said split voting was “certainly not the intention” but did not rule it out.

Senate hurdle

The tax plan sets income tax rates and other levies for next year, and must be passed in time for the tax office to bring in the changes. If it fails, the cabinet will almost certainly fall, NRC reported.

Earlier this week the cabinet offered about €350 million in concessions to opposition parties on the left and right, which have formed rival blocs and demanded that the coalition choose between them.

The coalition holds 66 of the 150 seats in parliament. It now looks likely to win next week’s vote with the help of the ChristenUnie, 50PLUS and the group led by former PVV MP Gidi Markuszower. But that is not enough in the senate, where it needs the support of either Pro and Volt or the BBB.

Left-wing parties attacked the coalition for relying on Markuszower, after MPs, including the coalition parties, voted earlier this year against deals with politicians who call for violence against refugees. Markuszower had said Palestinian refugees should be stopped “with maximum violence”, the Volkskrant reported. Pro, Denk and the PvdD said extra police funding credited to him amounted to buying his support.

Oosterhuis said there was “no agreement” with Markuszower, but added: “If Mr Markuszower wants to support the tax plan, I am not going to ask him to vote against it.”

Wealth tax offer

The Pro and Volt alliance used the debate to table an amendment that would shift €1.5 billion of tax from workers to the wealthiest. Income tax would be lowered, paid for by a higher tax rate on the largest fortunes, higher tax on business owners’ income from their companies and an end to tax breaks on passing on family businesses.

The VVD’s Wendy van Eijk said it was “unthinkable” that any coalition party would back the proposal “in this form”, and that her party would not support higher taxes on wealth.

Parliament votes on each amendment before voting on the plan as a whole. That means the VVD could vote against a wealth tax rise but still back the final plan, if D66 and the CDA help the amendment through.

MPs vote on the tax plan on November 12, and the senate in the week before Christmas.

item.title: Sunny end to week, but near-freezing nights ahead
item.description:
Sunny end to week, but near-freezing nights ahead

November 5, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Thursday and Friday will be sunny and dry across the Netherlands, but temperatures won’t rise past 10° and could drop close to freezing overnight, according to the KNMI forecast issued at 6am on Thursday.

The national weather institute KNMI said Thursday afternoon would bring plenty of sunshine, with a high of around 10°. Wind from the east will make it feel colder.

Thursday night will stay dry. Temperatures will fall to near freezing in the east, and stay at about 6° on the Wadden islands. Fog is possible in the far southwest.

Friday will be sunny and dry again. Highs will range from 8° in the far north to 12° in the southeast. Clouds will build in the southwest late in the afternoon.

Saturday may start with fog, mainly in the south and southwest, and some frost is possible inland, the KNMI said.

item.title: PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat
item.description:
PSV edged out by sharper Club Brugge in Champions League defeat

November 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

item.title: Police arrest “underground banker” in €60m money laundering case
item.description:
Police arrest “underground banker” in €60m money laundering case

November 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police have arrested a 55-year-old man from Rotterdam on suspicion of handling around €60 million in cash for a Turkish-German crime gang that smuggled gold to Turkey.

The man, who was detained in Eindhoven, was one of five people arrested in raids on October 7, police said on Wednesday. The other four were held in Germany. Police describe him as a suspected “underground banker”, an illegal financial intermediary.

Around 500 Dutch and German police and German customs officers took part in the operation, which was carried out with the support of Europol. The investigation began in October 2023, when German traffic police found several kilos of gold and almost €500,000 in cash hidden in a car on a motorway.

Rotterdam seaport police raided two properties in Rotterdam and Eindhoven, seizing data storage devices, around €10,000 in cash, a vehicle and real estate.

German police seized property worth at least €2 million, along with 19 vehicles, around €100,000 in cash and a “large quantity” of scrap gold and silver bars.

Police say the group funnelled tens of millions of euros a year to Turkey, probably the proceeds of drug dealing. The money was used to buy old gold through friendly jewellers, which was melted into bars and then smuggled to Turkey. An estimated 1 to 4 tonnes of gold, worth €55 million to €210 million, was smuggled over six years.

item.title: Singles and young professionals embrace urban courtyard living
item.description:
Partner content

Singles and young professionals embrace urban courtyard living

November 4, 2026

With half of Dutch people reporting feelings of loneliness, developments like ZAAM in Zaandam are highlighting the many advantages of living in a lively, green urban courtyard, where residents can enjoy more contact with their neighbours.

Loneliness is rising worldwide, and is also prevalent in the Netherlands, where authorities say social isolation carries health risks. “Those who experience it are more prone to illness and depression and generally report lower levels of happiness,” says the government.

Such loneliness, combined with high home prices and rents in large cities, has led to different forms of living that increasingly appeal to digital nomads and home workers, singles and single-parent families looking for more social contact.

“There’s a lot of loneliness and fear in today’s world,” says the real estate team at ZAAM. “People are looking for more contact.”

For singles, young professionals and anyone looking for a home that combines city convenience with a pleasant living environment, ZAAM offers an alternative to city-centre apartment living in Amsterdam.

ZAAM: green city living with room to connect

ZAAM is a new residential development in the heart of Zaandam, featuring apartments across two distinctive buildings, De Werf and De Zagerij. At its centre is a large, green inner courtyard, creating a welcoming outdoor space where residents can relax, enjoy nature and meet their neighbours.

“ZAAM combines the privacy and comfort of your own apartment with the benefits of living in a green, lively courtyard. It offers a sense of space and community that can be hard to find in a city apartment,” says the ZAAM Real Estate Team.

The apartments range from 39 to 72 square metres and are designed with modern living in mind. Each has at least one bedroom, a bright living area, a modern bathroom and a private balcony or terrace. All apartments are single-level and accessible by lift, making everyday living comfortable and convenient.

The ground-floor apartments, which feature impressive 4.15-metre-high ceilings and direct access to the lush green courtyard, are designed to create an exceptional sense of space and a unique connection with the outdoors.

The development also places an emphasis on sustainability and energy efficiency. Homes are gas-free and feature underfloor heating and cooling through a modern thermal energy system. High energy efficiency also means potentially lower energy bills, the team says.

Two city centres within easy reach

One of ZAAM’s biggest advantages is its location. Situated directly next to Zaandam railway station, the development puts Amsterdam Central Station just 10 minutes away by train. Zaandam’s own lively town centre, with its shops, restaurants and cafés, is also within easy walking distance.

“You really get the best of both worlds: the character and convenience of Zaandam, with Amsterdam practically on your doorstep. You can enjoy a quieter, greener living environment without giving up the advantages of the capital,” says the ZAAM Real Estate Team.

For international residents and young professionals, the location is particularly convenient, with excellent public transport connections and easy access to Amsterdam and the surrounding region.

And while the city is close, ZAAM is meant to offer a welcome change of pace. The green courtyard, private outdoor spaces and thoughtful apartment layouts create a comfortable home environment away from the bustle of the city.

Your new home before the end of the year

With construction nearing completion, the vast majority of ZAAM’s apartments have already been sold. Just a handful of homes remain available, including some  ground-floor apartments.

Buyers benefit from the advantages of new-build living: modern materials and appliances, energy-efficient installations, well-designed layouts and the reassurance of a brand-new home. Selected larger apartments also offer extra flexibility, with space for a home office, walk-in wardrobe or additional storage.

Parking spaces are also available for purchase with most apartments – a valuable extra in an area where parking can be a challenge.

You also won’t have to wait years to move in. Completion is planned for late 2026, meaning buyers can look forward to moving into their new home before the end of this year.

Only a limited number of apartments remain available, so anyone interested in securing a home at ZAAM is encouraged to get in touch soon.

Discover the remaining apartments at ZAAM and book your viewing today.

item.title: Netherlands nominate Klaas Knot to succeed ECB president Lagarde
item.description:
Netherlands nominate Klaas Knot to succeed ECB president Lagarde

November 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands has nominated former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot as a candidate to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank when she steps down next year.

Knot, 59, was president of De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) for 2011 to 2025. He was made a Grand Officer in the order of Oranje-Nassau, one of the Netherlands’ highest Dutch civilian honours, after retiring at the end of his second term.

Knot is seen as a front runner to become the second Dutch ECB president after Wim Duisenberg, who held the position from 1998 until 2003. His most serious rival is likely to be the former Spanish central bank president Pablo Hernández de Cos.

EU member states have until Friday to put forward candidates for the post, which Lagarde is leaving nine months before the end of her term. The nominations will be confirmed on Monday at a meeting of finance ministers.

The 70-year-old said she no longer “felt comfortable” with the requirement for European central bankers to be neutral in an increasingly polarised world, but has not given detailed reasons for her departure.

Reuters reported three weeks ago that the World Economic Forum, the Davos-based think tank, was lining her up as its next chair.

item.title: Anger after Maastricht university stops Jewish students’ meeting
item.description:
Anger after Maastricht university stops Jewish students’ meeting

November 4, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The University of Maastricht has been accused of “encouraging intimidation” after it cancelled a meeting by a Jewish students’ organisation at an hour’s notice because of protests outside the event.

Organisers said 12 students were due to attend a lecture by social sciences professor Eli Sapir titled Three Years after October 7, referring to the terrorist attacks by Hamas in Israel that triggered the destruction of Gaza.

The event was relocated at short notice after pro-Palestinian groups posted social media messages calling on people to demonstrate at the venue.

Protest group Maastricht Students for Palestine denounced the meeting as “Zionist propaganda” in an Instagram post, adding: “Bring your friends, something to cover your face, and some pots and spoons or drums to make some noise.”

University authorities decided to call off the event an hour before it was due to start after demonstrators appeared outside the new venue, even though the organisers said they were not acting aggressively.

In a statement, the university blamed pro-Israeli and pro-Palestinian groups for stoking tensions by appealing to their supporters to travel to Maastricht.

It said: “Because of online appeals by both supporters and opponents of the meeting with the aim of mobilising large numbers of people, the University could not guarantee its safety.”

But the organisers, the Jewish students’ union IJAR and campaign group StandWithUs Nederland, reacted furiously, accusing the university of “a systematic suppression of Jewish student life on campus”.

StandWithUs director Claudia van Zanten said: “I am absolutely furious that a small gathering of Jewish students was cancelled just before it was due to begin, without any legal justification whatsoever.

“By cancelling this lecture, the university is rewarding and encouraging intimidation.”

The group said it was considering taking further action against the university.
